checks.label: Laid along one at a time: 6 halves fit in 3, 8 quarters in 2, 8 tails of 3/4 m in 6 m, 4 in 3 m and 6 in 4 1/2 m, 3 pieces of 2/3 in 2, 6 eighths in 3/4, a tail and a third of one in 1 m, 2/3 of a 3/4 piece in 1/2 and 1 1/2 halves in 3/4; each matches flip and multiply and the one right option (cut by hand, exactly 4 tails, a 5th running past the end), and the pieces drawn over each amount add up to its length

Flip the fraction you divide by, its top and bottom swapped, and multiply, tops times tops over bottoms times bottoms: 2 × 3/2 = 6/2, 3/4 × 8 = 24/4, 1/2 × 4/3 = 4/6, 9/2 × 4/3 = 36/6 and 3/4 × 2 = 6/4. The wrong options are the slips: multiplying without the flip (4/3, 3/32, 3/8, 3 3/8), flipping the wrong number (1/3, 1/6, 3/2, 2/3), a quarter of 2 (1/2), one bar's 4 quarters, and 5 1/3, which leaves out the half metre

For amounts above 0, dividing by a number more than 1 gives less and by a fraction between 0 and 1 gives more: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 and 4 ÷ 1/2 = 8, as two pieces of 2 and eight halves fill four bars; of 10 ÷ 2 = 5, 10 × 1/2 = 5 and 10 ÷ 1/2 = 20, only 10 ÷ 1/2 is bigger than 10. At 0 and below it fails (0 ÷ 1/2 = 0; −4 ÷ 2 = −2, more; −4 ÷ 1/2 = −8, less), which is why the lesson says above 0
To divide with fractions, think about how many times a fraction will fit into a number or another fraction

Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, every answer's motion within 2.5 s, a tail cut or put back by hand within 0.8 s, counted pieces at least 0.2 s apart, and the = signs in 6 ÷ 3/4 = 6 × 4/3 = 8 only once the 3/4 has turned over
